title: Projection transformations of two compactifications agree under the refinement comparison
statement: Use the finite-field, coefficient, scheme and operation conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], with $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $c_1=(j_1,p_1)$, $c_2=(j_2,p_2)$ be two compactifications of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], so $j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i$ is an open immersion, $p_i:\overline X_i\to Y$ is proper and $p_ij_i=f$. Write $Rf_!^{c_i}=Rp_{i*}j_{i!}$ and $$\rho_{c_1,c_2}:Rf_!^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!^{c_2}$$ for the compactification comparison: at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ the natural isomorphism of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] (through a common refinement), on complexes with étale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]; at $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ its completed, rationalized and common-stage forms, on the coefficient domains on which [fix-lem-exchanges] (4) uses them. Let $\operatorname{PF}^{c_i}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!^{c_i}K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\to Rf_!^{c_i}(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L)$ be the projection transformations of [def-exchange-projection] for the compactifications $c_i$ (completed tensor and pullback at $\mathcal O_E$). Then for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] in these domains $$\rho_{c_1,c_2}(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L)\circ\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}_{f,K,L}=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}_{f,K,L}\circ\bigl(\rho_{c_1,c_2}(K)\otimes 1_L\bigr).$$ No invertibility of $\operatorname{PF}^{c_i}$ is asserted.

source.place: proof of prop-sf-pf-coherence, sentence "Independence of the compactification is the compatibility of the refinement comparisons with the counits and with $j_!$, together with naturality." proof.text: At finite coefficients set $T=K\otimes^L Lf^*L$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $Lf^*L$ is constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Apply [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](i), with its finite-Tor first factor $Lf^*L$ and bounded constructible second factor $K$, and tensor symmetry, to obtain $T\in D^b_c(X,A_n)$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), $T$ has an etale-origin witness. Use the witnessed input $K$ of the statement and this witnessed $T$ throughout the finite comparison calculation. Thus every comparison inverted below is on the domain of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]; no unrestricted compactification comparison on the unbounded pro-etale category is used.

source.place: Finite coefficient domains for K and K tensor Lf*L.

proof.text: We first work at a fixed finite coefficient $A_n$ in the ambient pro-etale categories, retaining the etale-origin witnesses wherever a comparison is inverted. Put $J_j=j_!$, $P_u=Lu^*$, $S_u=Ru_*$. Write $\gamma_j:J_jM\otimes N\to J_j(M\otimes P_jN)$ for the canonical open tensor map and $\pi_u:S_uM\otimes N\to S_u(M\otimes P_uN)$ for the ordinary counit projection. By [def-exchange-projection], $\operatorname{PF}^{(j,p)}=S_p\gamma_j\,\pi_p$, including $P_jP_p\cong P_f$. For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, put $a_M:J_{j_2}M\to S_uJ_{j_1}M$ for the proper/open comparison and $C_M:S_{p_1}J_{j_1}M\to S_{p_2}S_uJ_{j_1}M$ for direct-image composition. [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] identifies its comparison as $\theta_u=S_{p_2}(a^{-1})C$. Thus its inverse is $\sigma_u=C^{-1}S_{p_2}a$. The maps $a$ are the unit-normalized proper/open maps: [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization] fixes the finite pro-etale comparison as the transport of the finite proper/open map, and [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] fixes that map by the proper/open adjunction normalization (including the clopen section, rather than a Cartesian-square assumption).

source.place: Expand the specified projection and refinement transformations, with the directions fixed.

proof.text:
The counit formula for a composite gives its projection formula. Suppress the conjugate direct-image and pullback compositors of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), and let $M$ be on $\overline X_1$, $N$ on $Y$. Then
$$\pi_{p_2u;M,N}=S_{p_2}(\pi_{u;M,P_{p_2}N})\,\pi_{p_2;S_uM,N}.$$
Indeed, transpose the right-hand side under $P_uP_{p_2}\dashv S_{p_2}S_u$. Its transpose is
$$(\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1)\,\mu_{u;S_uM,P_{p_2}N}\,P_u((\varepsilon_{p_2,S_uM}\otimes1)\mu_{p_2;S_{p_2}S_uM,N}).$$
Naturality of $\mu_u$ moves $P_u\varepsilon_{p_2}$ to the first tensor factor. The counit becomes $\varepsilon_u\,P_u\varepsilon_{p_2}$ by [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), and the two $\mu$ factors become $\mu_{p_2u}$ by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. This is exactly the defining transpose of $\pi_{p_2u}$ in [def-exchange-projection]. The adjunction bijection proves the equality. The same three-line transpose calculation holds on the simultaneous derived system models, whose direct-image compositors are conjugate to the pullback compositors by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization].

source.place: Counit compatibility in the compactification-independence sentence; direct-image composition expanded.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-tensor-compatibility] to the commutative proper/open square with $U=W=X$, $r=1_X$, $V=\overline X_1$, $Z=\overline X_2$, $k_1=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $p=u$. It applies to this square even when $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ has an additional open-and-closed component: it does not require the square itself to be Cartesian. With $N=P_{p_2}L$ and $T=K\otimes P_fL$ it gives
$$a_T\,\gamma_{j_2;K,P_{p_2}L}
=S_u(\gamma_{j_1;K,P_{p_1}L})\,\pi_{u;J_{j_1}K,P_{p_2}L}\,(a_K\otimes1).$$
The pullback identifications are $P_{j_2}P_{p_2}\cong P_f\cong P_{j_1}P_uP_{p_2}$; the identity-map projection is identity by its unit/counit definition. This supplies the tensor compatibility of $a$, an assertion not supplied by mere functoriality of the compactification comparisons. The new lemma gives exactly the same equality in the derived category of coefficient systems, before taking any limit.

source.place: Compatibility with j_!: proper/open tensor square, specialized to a refinement.

proof.text:
Read all functors through $C$ and set $S=S_{p_2}$, $B=S_u$, $M=J_{j_1}K$. In these coordinates $\sigma_u=S(a)$, and step 3 writes $\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}=SB(\gamma_{j_1})\,S(\pi_u)\,\pi_{p_2;BM,L}$. Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}(\sigma_{u,K}\otimes1)
&=SB(\gamma_{j_1})S(\pi_u)\pi_{p_2;BM,L}(S(a_K)\otimes1)\\
&=S\bigl(B(\gamma_{j_1})\pi_u(a_K\otimes1)\bigr)\pi_{p_2;J_{j_2}K,L}\\
&=S(a_T\gamma_{j_2})\pi_{p_2;J_{j_2}K,L}
=\sigma_{u,T}\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second line is naturality of the counit-defined $\pi_{p_2}$ in its first argument; the third is step 4. Reinserting the conjugate compositors gives the equality for the specified $\sigma_u$, not for an arbitrary functor isomorphism. Since $\sigma_u=\theta_u^{-1}$ on the witnessed domain of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], multiplication by $\theta_{u,T}$ on the left and by $\theta_{u,K}\otimes1$ on the right gives $\theta_{u,T}\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}(\theta_{u,K}\otimes1)$. Only a refinement comparison is inverted here.

source.place: Paste the explicit proper/open square with the proper counit-projection composite.

proof.text:
Choose a common refinement $d$ of $c_1,c_2$ by [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], with comparisons $t_i:Rf_!^d\to Rf_!^{c_i}$. Write $P_d,P_i$ for their projection maps and evaluate comparison subscripts at $K$ or $T=K\otimes P_fL$. Step 5 gives $t_{i,T}P_d=P_i(t_{i,K}\otimes1)$. The prescribed comparison is $\rho=t_2t_1^{-1}$ by the same coherence theorem. Consequently
$$\rho_TP_1=t_{2,T}t_{1,T}^{-1}P_1=t_{2,T}P_d(t_{1,K}^{-1}\otimes1)=P_2(t_{2,K}t_{1,K}^{-1}\otimes1)=P_2(\rho_K\otimes1).$$
This is precisely the desired finite-coefficient equality. Choice independence and the cocycle law identify this comparison with the stated $\rho$; they are not being used as a substitute for the projection calculation.

source.place: Remove the choice through a common refinement.

proof.text: At the integral stage, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives uniformly finite-Tor reductions for both $K$ and $L$. Use their normalized derived systems in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. We verify its intermediate-domain condition. Open extension on systems is exact. Its cohomology has the same finite constructible stratification on the open and zero on the closed complement; adjoining that complement shows constructibility without changing the cohomological interval. The open tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], applied to coefficient quotients, shows $J_j(M)_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\cong J_j(M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\cong J_j(M_n)$, hence normalization. The same tensor comparison with an arbitrary coefficient-module sheaf shows that open extension preserves Tor bounds: restrict the sheaf, tensor on the open, and extend the resulting cohomology, which is zero outside the prescribed interval. Its finite levels have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Proper direct images have uniform cohomological bounds and constructibility by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]; the completed pullback and tensor outputs are constructible by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]. For those integral outputs, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] again supplies uniform finite-level Tor bounds. The proper and open operations on their normalized systems are exactly the realizations in the cited realization lemma. Consequently every intermediate expression in the refinement calculation satisfies that lemma's bounds. This uses no finite-Tor assumption added to $K$: it is a consequence of its integral constructibility over the DVR.

All schemes in a compactification or refinement are finite type over the field, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Their open immersions are thus quasi-compact. By [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], open extension preserves completeness, and its completed comparison is the specified one from strict finite open-extension diagrams. Retain the compatible etale-origin witnesses at all finite reductions required by the integral domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Repeat steps 3-5 as an identity in the derived category of systems, using [lem-sf-proper-open-tensor-compatibility] in that category. By [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], the realization isomorphisms intertwine the units, counits, open maps, tensor and composition maps, proper/open comparisons, and their whiskerings. Applying its total-limit functor to that actual system identity therefore gives the integral refinement identity with the completed tensor and pullback of the statement. The common-refinement algebra of step 6 then applies to the completed comparisons of [fix-lem-exchanges](4), giving the integral assertion. No equality of integral maps is deduced merely from equality at finite levels.

source.place: Realization of the derived-system identity with all specified maps.

proof.text: At $E$, apply the raw scalar-localization functor to the integral equality. By [def-exchange-projection] the rational projection map is exactly the image of its integral composite, and [fix-lem-exchanges](4) uses the same rationalized refinement comparisons. A functor preserves the displayed composition and tensor comparisons, so it sends the proved equality to the required rational equality, including morphisms written with a scalar denominator. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the two inputs and the finitely many maps in the square at one common finite coefficient field, as in [def-exchange-projection] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The rational equality there gives equality of the represented morphism classes. Enlarging the field carries the specified units, counits, open tensor and comparison maps to their specified counterparts by the scalar-extension data in [def-exchange-projection]; hence the equality is independent of this common presentation. This proves all stated coefficient stages without an assertion that finite evaluations detect equality of integral maps, and without inverting either projection map.
